claims.text: Active learning can generate MLIP training sets tailored to a specified class of systems and properties while requiring a minimal number of DFT calculations.
An actively learned MLIP can replace most explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics sampling at substantially lower computational cost.
Uncertainty-guided retraining can identify configurations for which additional ab initio calculations are needed.
The proposed on-the-fly validation module can specifically detect deviations in electron–vibration coupling.
On-the-fly ab initio corrections can correct electron–vibration coupling anomalies during phase transitions.
The correction scheme can retrieve an accurate energy landscape whenever the MLIP has high uncertainty.
Accurate representation of local bonding environments, vibrational spectra, and coordination fluctuations is sufficient to capture the relevant anharmonic and electron–vibration effects.
The combined MLIP and correction method can preserve vibrational-entropy contributions to phase free energies.
The combined method can preserve anharmonic contributions to phase free energies.
The combined method can produce faithful free energies for both solid and liquid phases.
The method is applicable to elemental and binary metals such as Ni, Fe, and Fe–Cr from 0.8Tm to 1.2Tm at zero pressure.
Application to higher-complexity multicomponent systems may require additional validation of electron–vibration coupling corrections.
The proposed workflow will accelerate free-energy evaluation by roughly one order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD.
The proposed workflow will achieve phase free-energy errors of no more than about 5% relative to TOR-TILD or full-AIMD benchmarks.
Melting temperatures and latent heats produced by the proposed workflow will agree with benchmark values within about 5%.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluations are accurate but computationally very expensive.
TOR-TILD is an accurate but computationally very expensive free-energy workflow.
